question: Which Five-Year Plan aimed to achieve self-reliance and aimed at 'growth with stability'?
solution:
The correct answer is __**Fourth Plan**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The **Fourth Five-Year Plan (1969-1974)** aimed to achieve **self-reliance** and emphasized **growth with stability** in India’s economy.
 
• This plan focused on **increased industrial production** and **reducing dependence on foreign imports** by encouraging domestic production.
 
• It aimed to strengthen the agriculture sector while promoting technological advancements, particularly in heavy industries and infrastructure.
 
• The goal was to enhance the overall economic structure, reduce poverty, and improve social and industrial development.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• The Fourth Plan was introduced under the leadership of Prime Minister **Indira Gandhi**, during a period of political instability and a focus on strengthening national unity.
 
• **Self-reliance** was a key theme, as India sought to reduce its dependence on foreign aid and promote indigenous growth in sectors such as agriculture, manufacturing, and defense.
 
• The Fourth Plan also saw efforts in the **Green Revolution**, aimed at increasing agricultural productivity, especially in staple crops like wheat and rice.
 
• Despite these efforts, the plan faced challenges like the **Indo-Pakistani War of 1971** and an energy crisis that hindered its full success.
 
• The focus on growth with stability continued in subsequent plans, but the Fourth Plan marked a crucial step in India’s journey toward economic self-sufficiency.
 
• Subsequent Five-Year Plans shifted focus, such as the **Sixth Plan** (1980-1985), which prioritized poverty alleviation and employment generation.
